description: Separate automatic recovery allowance from immutable task recovery configuration so a bounded recovery round remains auditable and manual retry starts a fresh full-budget round.

tasks.title: Implement immutable workflow recovery rounds with manual retry reset
tasks.description: Implement `recoveryRemaining` as separate task-attempt state across the server workflow domain, persisted run state, internal work/dispatch/report contracts, runner connection types, and `tryRecovery`, while keeping `RecoveryDefinition` unchanged and the runner as the state interpretation and mutation authority. Centralize task definition projection and distinct fresh/continuation construction so fresh tasks carry explicit null, automatic self-retries preserve the declaration and carry remaining minus one, and absent continuation state fails closed. Normalize pre-change persisted recovery chains with presence-aware raw JSON migration, align `design/workflow/recovery.md`, and include focused server and runner regression coverage in the same delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: `RecoveryDefinition` and `TaskDefinition.Recovery` remain declaration-only; nullable `TaskRun.RecoveryRemaining` stores separate attempt state, explicit null marks a fresh recovery-enabled attempt, and numeric continuation values are bounded between 0 and the declared budget.

A single task definition projection lists the definition-owned fields and excludes attempt identity, lifecycle status, timestamps, worker/work ids, output, provenance, and `RecoveryRemaining`; stage initialization, ordinary runtime insertion, and manual retry use fresh-null construction, while automatic continuation construction requires an explicit numeric value.

`recoveryRemaining` is carried without loss through `WorkflowTaskWork`, the task variant of `WorkItem`, `WorkDispatch`, `WorkDispatchResponse`, runner `RenderedWorkItem`, runner `AddTaskInput`, and `RuntimeTaskInput` in report `addTasks`; every runner-produced follow-up with a recovery declaration carries an explicit value, and new Orleans field ids are appended without reusing or renumbering existing ids.

`WorkflowWorkLifecycle`, `WorkflowItemTranslator`, Runner poll/report DTO mapping, and runner connection mapping preserve explicit null versus numeric state; poll serialization emits explicit null and TypeScript keeps it distinct from absent/undefined; `ActionContext`, workflow YAML, public task APIs, CLI, and Web DTOs do not gain recovery-budget state.

Runner `tryRecovery` interprets explicit null as the declared budget, treats an absent property as ineligible, never rewrites `recovery.budget`, consumes exactly one allowance only when a handler matches, and emits a self-retry with unchanged recovery configuration plus `recoveryRemaining - 1`.

Malformed remaining state cannot expand a round: negative input is clamped to 0 and permits no automatic recovery, above-budget input is clamped to the declared budget, and runner-produced recovery-enabled follow-ups missing or null state are rejected by the report/insertion path.

With declared budget 2 and matching output on attempts with remaining 2, 1, and 0, exactly two recovery sequences are scheduled, generated self-retries carry 1 and 0, and the zero-remaining attempt schedules no handler task or self-retry and retains its ordinary result.

Existing recovery semantics remain unchanged: handlers are evaluated in declaration order using `field=value`, only the first match runs, matching is independent of completed/failed status, handler tasks retain declaration order, each recovery-enabled handler task carries its own explicit full numeric allowance, `retrySelf: true` appends self-retry last, `retrySelf: false` appends no self-retry, and unmatched output consumes no allowance.

After an automatic round exhausts budget 2 and fails at remaining 0, `mo issue retry` creates a new task attempt with the unchanged declaration and explicit null fresh state; the runner evaluates it at allowance 2, the same output can run two further recovery sequences, and every prior attempt remains unchanged.

Presence-aware raw JSON migration distinguishes a missing legacy property from new-format explicit null/zero. A legacy 2, 1, 0 chain with otherwise-equivalent declarations is normalized to one budget-2 declaration plus numeric remaining 2, 1, 0, while explicit null/zero is unchanged on repeated loads and structurally ambiguous reused definition ids are rejected rather than rewritten.

Workflow run JSON persistence round-trips explicit-null and numeric `RecoveryRemaining` with no EF schema migration, persists normalized legacy state on the next save, and task history/config projections expose the workflow-declared recovery budget and handlers rather than consumed values.

`design/workflow/recovery.md` documents `recoveryRemaining`, immutable recovery configuration, and manual retry as a new round; examples no longer decrement `recovery.budget` inside generated self-retries.

Runner coverage in `packages/runner/tests/executor-recovery.spec.ts` verifies explicit-null initialization, immutable declaration, decrement, zero allowance, absent-state fail-closed behavior, negative/above-budget clamps, no-match behavior, first-handler selection, completed-result matching, nested recovery-enabled handler initialization, both `retrySelf` branches, and follow-up order; `npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass.

Server domain, translator/contract, persistence, and workflow grain specs verify fresh-null versus numeric-continuation construction, explicit-null poll serialization, rejection of missing/null runner continuation state, end-to-end pass-through, JSON presence detection and idempotence, legacy normalization and ambiguity rejection, budget exhaustion, and manual retry reset without real network, runner process, external database, or wall-clock time; `npm run build` and `npm test` pass.
tasks.output: Server Workflow task-attempt state and internal runner contracts updated with `recoveryRemaining`; runner recovery evaluation preserves immutable declarations; manual retry restores the full budget; recovery design documentation and server/runner regression suites are green.
tasks.notes: This is intentionally one atomic functional task: the server domain state, server-runner contract, and runner evaluator are tightly coupled and mixed old/new execution is unsupported. Follow design Decisions 1-6; do not place remaining state inside `RecoveryDefinition`, do not initialize numeric allowance in the control plane, preserve explicit null on fresh dispatch, never treat an absent continuation as fresh, and do not split tests into a separate task. Legacy normalization stays in presence-aware raw workflow JSON migration and requires no EF or public API/schema change.
